To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface structure of SrO-terminated SrTiO3 is a 1 × 2 reconstruction and that the structure is determined by the surface rearrangement of edge-sharing TiO6-x blocks.
the surface structure of a model perovskite is determined by a surface rearrangement of edge-sharing TiO6-x octahedra.
the structure and chemistry of SrTiO 3 surfaces is determined by the formation of edge-sharing TiO 5 blocks at the surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and chemistry of SrTiO(3) (001) and how it relates to other perovskite oxide surfaces.
the development of new materials and processes for the fabrication and application of thin oxide films.
the development of new concepts and methodologies for the prediction of the structure and chemistry of oxide surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TiO2 surface is a TiO2-rich one, and that the TiO6-x octahedra are edge sharing.
the surface of SrTi O3 (100) is Ti rich, and that the Ti-rich surface is a result of a rearrangement of Ti atoms in the topmost layer.
the surface structure of the perovskite SrTiO3(001) is determined by the formation of a surface layer with a TiO2 stoichiometry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface structure of Sr-rich perovskites can be understood in terms of a reduction of Couloumb repulsion, whereas for TiO2-rich surfaces, the dominant factor is minimization of ‘surface dipoles’.
we have solved the 2×1 surface structure of SrO-terminated SrTiO3(001) by a combination of high resolution electron microscopy and theoretical methods.
the surface structure of Sr-rich SrTiO3 is determined by a combination of Coulombic forces, minimization of ‘surface energy’ (surface stress), and the tendency to form TiO6 octahedra.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface structure of a perovskites is not controlled by Coulomb forces or charge transfer.
the surface structure of SrO-deficient SrTiO3 can be described by a model in which TiO6-x octahedral units rearrange into blocks of edge-sharing TiO6 units.
the structure of the surface of SrTi O3 is determined by a reduction of Coulom b forces, and that the TiO6-x octahedral units play an important role in determining the surface structure.
